AI.tldr: This paper reviews the field of spin-based quantum batteries, covering charging and work-extraction protocols, the effects of external factors on performance, the connection between continuously and periodically driven spin chains via Floquet engineering, and experimental realizations and proposals for current and near-term quantum technologies.
AI.motivation: Advances in quantum information and thermodynamics have opened new pathways for energy storage at the microscopic scale, and quantum batteries present a conceptual alternative to conventional macroscopic chemical batteries. The authors aim to provide a comprehensive review of spin-based quantum batteries, their fundamental protocols, and their practical implementation pathways.
AI.method: The paper is a review that navigates the landscape of established spin-based quantum batteries, examines existing charging and work-extraction protocols, analyzes the impact of external factors on battery performance, establishes connections between continuously and periodically driven spin chains (motivated by Floquet-engineered proposals) as platforms for quantum energy storage, and surveys experimental realizations and proposals.
AI.result: The review maps the current state of spin-based quantum batteries, highlights how quantum coherence, correlations, and many-body dynamics enable energy storage, and evaluates the implementability and scalability of experimental proposals in current and near-term quantum technologies.
AI.conclusion: Quantum batteries leveraging spin systems offer a viable conceptual alternative to conventional batteries, and the connection between Floquet-engineered and continuously driven spin chains provides a promising route toward practical quantum energy storage, with experimental feasibility in near-term quantum devices.

title: Scaling theory of decoherence in Dicke superradiance
summary: The survival of many-body coherence depends on the competition between correlation buildup and decoherence. In Dicke superradiance, collective emission builds up correlations, producing a peak intensity scaling as $N^2$ for $N$ emitters. We develop a scaling theory including local dephasing and spontaneous emission and obtain fully collective, partially collective, and independent-emitter scaling regimes. The boundary of the fully collective regime defines a continuous phase transition in a transient observable. Local decoherence can prevent $N^2$ scaling despite increasing $N$.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a scaling theory for Dicke superradiance under local dephasing and spontaneous emission, identifying fully collective, partially collective, and independent-emitter scaling regimes. It reveals that the fully collective regime boundary constitutes a continuous phase transition in a transient observable, and that local decoherence can suppress N² scaling even for large emitter numbers.
AI.motivation: To understand how local decoherence competes with collective correlation buildup in many-body coherent systems, specifically determining when Dicke superradiance's N² intensity scaling survives under realistic decoherence conditions.
AI.method: Development of a scaling theory that incorporates local dephasing and spontaneous emission to map out distinct scaling regimes (fully collective, partially collective, and independent-emitter) and analyze the phase transition at the boundary of the fully collective regime.
AI.result: Identification of three scaling regimes characterized by different superradiant behavior, with the fully collective regime bounded by a continuous phase transition in a transient observable. Demonstrates that local decoherence can prevent N² scaling regardless of how large N becomes.
AI.conclusion: Local decoherence fundamentally limits collective enhancement in Dicke superradiance, and the transient phase transition structure provides a framework for predicting when N² scaling is achievable.

title: Slow-light-enhanced Atomic Frequency Comb Quantum Memory in Stoichiometric EuCl$_3 \cdot$ 6D$_2$O
summary: Rare-earth-doped crystals are promising candidates for quantum storage, yet their performance in free-space configurations is fundamentally restricted by low optical depth. Here, we demonstrate high-efficiency quantum storage in a stoichiometric EuCl$_3 \cdot$ 6D$_2$O crystal, which intrinsically provides high optical density without the complexity of cavity implementation. We show that in this high-density regime, the system exhibits significant slow-light-like effects, including dispersion-induced echo delays and finesse-dependent echo intensity modulation. We develop a unified theoretical framework showing how absorption and dispersion work in concert to mediate echo generation. We achieve storage efficiencies of 42.9% for classical light and 34.4% for weak coherent pulses, alongside 90% efficiency for slow-light storage. These findings validate EuCl$_3 \cdot$ 6D$_2$O as a robust platform, establishing a viable pathway for scalable solid-state quantum memory.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates high-efficiency quantum storage in a stoichiometric EuCl3·6D2O crystal, which intrinsically provides high optical density without cavity complexity. They achieve 42.9% storage efficiency for classical light, 34.4% for weak coherent pulses, and 90% for slow-light storage, while developing a unified theoretical framework for absorption-dispersion-mediated echo generation.
AI.motivation: Rare-earth-doped crystals are promising for quantum storage but suffer from fundamentally restricted performance in free-space configurations due to low optical depth. The authors aim to overcome this limitation without the complexity of cavity implementation.
AI.method: The authors use a stoichiometric EuCl3·6D2O crystal that intrinsically provides high optical density. They develop a unified theoretical framework showing how absorption and dispersion work in concert to mediate echo generation, and characterize slow-light-like effects including dispersion-induced echo delays and finesse-dependent echo intensity modulation.
AI.result: They achieve storage efficiencies of 42.9% for classical light, 34.4% for weak coherent pulses, and 90% for slow-light storage in the high-density regime.
AI.conclusion: The findings validate EuCl3·6D2O as a robust platform for scalable solid-state quantum memory, establishing a viable pathway that avoids cavity complexity while achieving high storage efficiency.

title: Deterministic QKD source robust against side-channel attacks
summary: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is secure in principle, but practical security can be undermined by discrepancies between real devices and the idealized models assumed in security proofs. Source side channels, including those exploited by Trojan-horse attacks, are particularly detrimental: neglecting them compromises implementation security, whereas accounting for them reduces performance. Here we propose a QKD source that is intrinsically robust against side-channel attacks. Unlike existing passive and modulator-free schemes, it requires neither post-selection of the emitted pulses nor devices with a perfect extinction ratio to suppress side channels, and it does not introduce correlations between the intensity and the encoded bit or basis. Consequently, simpler security proofs apply directly, yielding substantially higher key rates. Our proposal appears to be within reach of current technology and therefore provides a clear and practical path toward implementation-secure QKD.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a QKD source intrinsically robust against side-channel attacks (including Trojan-horse attacks), avoiding post-selection and perfect extinction ratio requirements while eliminating intensity-bit correlations, leading to simpler security proofs and higher key rates.
AI.motivation: Practical security of QKD is undermined by discrepancies between real devices and idealized security-proof models. Source side channels, especially those exploited by Trojan-horse attacks, either compromise security if neglected or degrade performance if accounted for.
AI.method: The authors propose a new QKD source design that is intrinsically robust against side-channel attacks. Unlike existing passive and modulator-free schemes, it requires no post-selection of emitted pulses and no devices with perfect extinction ratio, and introduces no correlations between intensity and encoded bit or basis.
AI.result: The proposed source enables simpler security proofs to be applied directly, yielding substantially higher key rates. The scheme appears feasible with current technology.
AI.conclusion: The proposal provides a clear and practical path toward implementation-secure QKD, addressing the fundamental trade-off between security and performance in practical QKD systems.

title: Approximate sampling from decoded quantum interferometry via Markov chain Monte Carlo methods
summary: Optimization problems are among the leading candidates for industrially relevant quantum advantage. Decoded quantum interferometry (DQI) has been proposed to tackle approximate optimization, establishing a connection to classical decoding problems. While previous work has primarily focused on the theoretical complexity of DQI, comparatively little is known about its empirical performance relative to classical algorithms. In this work, we shed further light on the complexity of DQI and investigate numerically whether classical sampling methods can emulate the optimization capabilities of DQI. We first present a simplified analytical characterization of DQI that connects its expected performance to binomial statistics, and we identify concrete obstacles in further studying the complexity of DQI. Exploiting the fact that DQI output probabilities are efficiently computable, we apply Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques, particularly block-Gibbs sampling, to sample from the induced distribution. We study the runtime scaling of these methods for two optimization problems called max-XORSAT, where we reach beyond $1000$ effective qubits; and OPI, where we reach beyond $150$ effective qubits. Our results show that MCMC algorithms can reliably attain the approximation ratios expected from DQI across a broad range of problem sizes. In OPI, in the regime where a super-polynomial advantage is claimed for DQI, we observe an empirical runtime for MCMC that scales approximately as $1.1^{n}$, indicating exponential growth with a comparatively small base. Our findings do not refute existing quantum advantage claims but provide new empirical evidence that classical sampling algorithms can closely match DQI's optimization performance, offering a more nuanced perspective on the practical advantage of DQI.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the empirical performance of Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) for approximate optimization, showing that classical Markov chain Monte Carlo methods, particularly block-Gibbs sampling, can closely match DQI's optimization capabilities. The authors provide a simplified analytical characterization of DQI, study runtime scaling on max-XORSAT and OPI problems, and find that classical sampling achieves DQI's approximation ratios with exponential scaling having a small base (~1.1^n) in OPI's claimed super-polynomial advantage regime.
AI.motivation: While DQI was proposed as a leading candidate for industrially relevant quantum advantage in approximate optimization, previous work focused primarily on theoretical complexity with little known about its empirical performance relative to classical algorithms. The authors aim to fill this gap by investigating whether classical sampling methods can emulate DQI's optimization capabilities.
AI.method: The authors present a simplified analytical characterization of DQI connecting its expected performance to binomial statistics. Exploiting that DQI output probabilities are efficiently computable, they apply Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) techniques, specifically block-Gibbs sampling, to sample from the induced distribution. They study runtime scaling on max-XORSAT (beyond 1000 effective qubits) and OPI (beyond 150 effective qubits) optimization problems.
AI.result: MCMC algorithms reliably attain the approximation ratios expected from DQI across a broad range of problem sizes. For OPI, in the regime where super-polynomial advantage is claimed for DQI, the empirical runtime for MCMC scales approximately as 1.1^n, indicating exponential growth with a comparatively small base. The findings do not refute quantum advantage claims but show classical sampling can closely match DQI's optimization performance.
AI.conclusion: The results provide new empirical evidence that classical sampling algorithms can closely match DQI's optimization performance, offering a more nuanced perspective on the practical advantage of DQI. The paper does not refute existing quantum advantage claims but highlights that the practical gap between quantum and classical approaches may be narrower than previously understood.

title: Efficient atom rearrangements for quantum error correction primitives with a single AOD
summary: Neutral-atom quantum computers offer arbitrary connectivity enabled by atom transport. Some logical operations can then be simplified or reduced entirely to geometric rearrangements of the atoms. Minimizing the duration of these movements is therefore essential for high logical throughput. We introduce new primitives to shear, rotate and reflect 2D arrays of atoms in a static lattice using sweeps of a single dynamic crossed acousto-optic deflector (AOD) pair. Using (nega-)binary and geometric decompositions, we achieve an AOD stroke count scaling logarithmically in the linear size of the array. In one example, we use the Paeth decomposition to implement a $90^{\circ}$ rotation for a transversal Hadamard gate in a rotated surface code of distance $d$ in $3\lfloor\log_2(d-1)\rfloor + 4$ AOD strokes and $O(d^{1/3})$ constant-jerk time, against $O(d^2)$ strokes and $O(d^{7/3})$ time for atom-by-atom rearrangement.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces new primitives for shearing, rotating, and reflecting 2D arrays of neutral atoms in a static lattice using sweeps of a single dynamic crossed acousto-optic deflector (AOD) pair. Using (nega-)binary and geometric decompositions, the stroke count scales logarithmically in the linear size of the array, significantly improving over atom-by-atom rearrangement. For example, a 90° rotation for a transversal Hadamard gate in a rotated surface code of distance d uses only 3⌊log2(d−1)⌋+4 AOD strokes and O(d^{1/3}) constant-jerk time, versus O(d²) strokes and O(d^{7/3}) time for atom-by-atom rearrangement.
AI.motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computers exploit atom transport for arbitrary connectivity, but minimizing movement duration is critical for high logical throughput. Existing atom-by-atom rearrangement approaches are inefficient, motivating more efficient geometric primitives for array manipulation.
AI.method: The authors introduce new primitives for shearing, rotating, and reflecting 2D atomic arrays using sweeps from a single dynamic crossed AOD pair. They apply (nega-)binary and geometric decompositions (including the Paeth decomposition) to achieve logarithmic scaling of the AOD stroke count with respect to the linear array size.
AI.result: The proposed approach achieves logarithmic AOD stroke scaling in the linear array size. For a 90° rotation enabling a transversal Hadamard gate in a rotated surface code of distance d, only 3⌊log2(d−1)⌋+4 strokes and O(d^{1/3}) constant-jerk time are needed, compared to O(d²) strokes and O(d^{7/3}) time for atom-by-atom rearrangement.
AI.conclusion: The logarithmic stroke count and significantly reduced movement time demonstrate a major improvement in efficiency for geometric manipulation of neutral-atom arrays, enabling higher logical throughput in neutral-atom quantum computers.

title: Entanglement Swapping with Integrated Narrowband Photon Sources for Quantum Repeaters
summary: Promising implementations of first generation quantum repeaters are predicted to require atomic-based quantum memory systems interfaced with photonic sources. Integrated photonics provides a promising solution for fibre-based, field-deployed operation of quantum repeaters, however many leading quantum memory platforms require narrow-bandwidth photons that are challenging to generate with integrated photonics. Narrowband photons also present significant technical challenges when implementing entanglement-swapping, particularly with regards to systems-level stabilisation. This work addresses some of these fundamental and technical challenges, by demonstrating entanglement-swapping using state-of-the-art integrated photon sources with bandwidths compatible with multiple atomic-based quantum memory platforms. We obtained a background-subtracted (net) HOM visibility of 0.99$\,\pm\,$0.01, showing high photon indistinguishability and purity, with a net swapped state visibility of $\mathcal{V}$=0.88$\,\pm\,$0.06 demonstrating that the final entanglement would be sufficient to violate a Bell inequality. The experiment used independent pump lasers for each photon pair source, with highly different frequencies to mimic entanglement swapping between different repeater nodes or platforms. Phase and frequency stabilisation spanning 1.6 THz was achieved using all-fibre, commercially-available components. These results address important challenges in implementing field-deployed quantum repeaters, from the integrated photonic solutions for narrowband photon pairs, to systems-level stabilisation between independent quantum repeater nodes.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement-swapping using integrated photonic sources generating narrowband photons compatible with atomic quantum memory platforms. The authors achieved a net HOM visibility of 0.99±0.01 and a swapped state visibility of 0.88±0.06 (sufficient to violate a Bell inequality) using independent pump lasers with 1.6 THz frequency separation, with all-fibre phase/frequency stabilisation using commercially-available components.
AI.motivation: First-generation quantum repeaters require atomic-based quantum memory interfaced with photonic sources. Integrated photonics is promising for field deployment, but leading quantum memory platforms need narrowband photons that are difficult to generate with integrated sources, and narrowband photons complicate entanglement-swapping due to systems-level stabilisation challenges.
AI.method: The authors demonstrated entanglement-swapping using state-of-the-art integrated photon sources producing narrowband photons compatible with multiple atomic quantum memory platforms. They used independent pump lasers at highly different frequencies to emulate swapping between different repeater nodes/platforms, and achieved phase and frequency stabilisation spanning 1.6 THz using all-fibre, commercially-available components.
AI.result: A background-subtracted (net) HOM visibility of 0.99±0.01 was obtained, demonstrating high photon indistinguishability and purity. The net swapped state visibility was V=0.88±0.06, sufficient to violate a Bell inequality, confirming the final entanglement quality.
AI.conclusion: The work addresses key challenges for field-deployed quantum repeaters, including integrated photonic solutions for narrowband photon pair generation and systems-level stabilisation between independent quantum repeater nodes.

title: Purifications for Convex Cones
summary: Motivated by the importance of the purification principle in quantum theory and generalized probabilistic theories, we study purifications using only the geometry of a finite-dimensional proper convex cone. We prove an existence theorem for indecomposable cones and intermediate tensor cones containing the maximally entangled state; in particular, every interior point of an indecomposable homogeneous cone admits a purification. This applies to Lorentz cones, for example. We also give a criterion for uniqueness up to local automorphisms. On the boundary, we show that if every proper face of $C$ is simplicial, then only pure points can admit purifications, and we demonstrate that this conclusion fails in the presence of non-simplicial faces. Examples involving positive semidefinite cones, Lorentz cones, $k$-positive maps, PPT tensors, and polyhedral cones illustrate both existence and non-uniqueness phenomena.

AI.tldr: This paper studies purifications of states in quantum theory and generalized probabilistic theories using only the geometry of finite-dimensional proper convex cones. It proves existence of purifications for indecomposable cones and intermediate tensor cones containing the maximally entangled state, gives a uniqueness criterion up to local automorphisms, and analyzes boundary behavior showing that non-simplicial faces can admit non-trivial purifications.
AI.motivation: The purification principle is central to quantum theory and generalized probabilistic theories. The authors aim to understand when and how states can be purified using purely geometric properties of convex cones, without relying on the full algebraic structure of quantum mechanics.
AI.method: The paper uses convex geometry and cone theory. It proves an existence theorem for indecomposable cones and intermediate tensor cones containing the maximally entangled state, establishes a uniqueness criterion via local automorphisms, and analyzes boundary cases where all proper faces are simplicial vs. cases with non-simplicial faces.
AI.result: Every interior point of an indecomposable homogeneous cone (e.g., Lorentz cones) admits a purification. Uniqueness up to local automorphisms is characterized. If every proper face of a cone is simplicial, only pure points admit purifications; this fails in the presence of non-simplicial faces. Examples from positive semidefinite cones, Lorentz cones, k-positive maps, PPT tensors, and polyhedral cones illustrate both existence and non-uniqueness.
AI.conclusion: The geometric framework of convex cones provides both existence and uniqueness/non-uniqueness criteria for purifications, with simplicial nature of faces playing a key role in determining boundary behavior.

title: Quantum Arago-Fresnel interference of displaced spin states of photons
summary: The four laws by Arago and Fresnel distinguish the coplanarity of two light beams to determine their capacity of interference, laying the historic milestone for conceptualizing the polarization of light. Equipped with modern descriptions of non-classical states, we re-investigate the macroscopic Arago-Fresnel interference producible by photon helicities. To this end, we compute the Stokes parameter of a polarized beam combined from a regular coherent state (displaced from the vacuum) and a displaced single-photon spin state (displaced from either a left- or right-spin state of photon). The spin orientation, together with its relative asymmetry with respect to the polarizing orientation of the displacing coherent state, produces distinguishing parameter dependences and thus distict interference fringes. Conversely, this quantum interferometry establishes a purely optical method to determine the spin of an unknown incident photon.

AI.tldr: The paper re-investigates Arago-Fresnel interference using modern quantum optics, computing Stokes parameters for beams formed by combining a coherent state with a displaced single-photon spin state. The spin orientation and its asymmetry relative to the coherent state's polarization produce distinct interference fringes, enabling a purely optical method to determine the spin of an unknown photon.
AI.motivation: To revisit the historic Arago-Fresnel laws—which define the coplanarity condition for light interference and conceptually founded the notion of light polarization—using modern non-classical state descriptions, thereby exploring quantum enhancements to classical interferometry and photon spin determination.
AI.method: The authors compute the Stokes parameter of a polarized beam formed by superposing a regular coherent state (displaced from vacuum) with a displaced single-photon spin state (displaced from either a left- or right-spin photon state). They analyze how the spin orientation and its relative asymmetry with respect to the displacing coherent field lead to distinct parameter dependences and interference fringes.
AI.result: The spin orientation and its asymmetry relative to the polarizing coherent state generate distinguishing parameter dependences, yielding distinct interference fringes for different photon spin states.
AI.conclusion: This quantum interferometric scheme provides a purely optical method to determine the spin (helicity) of an unknown incident photon, extending the classic Arago-Fresnel framework into the quantum domain.

title: Optimal T Counts under Sparsity: from QROM to State Preparation and Block Encoding

AI.tldr: This paper initiates the study of the T-count (non-Clifford gate) cost of sparse quantum read-only memory (QROM), proving asymptotically optimal Θ(√sm + √sn) T-count bounds for accessing s nonzero entries among 2^n addresses. Upper bounds use multilevel hashing, while lower bounds reduce sparse QROM to state preparation and employ counting arguments for adaptive Clifford+T circuits. The results yield matching T-count bounds for s-sparse state preparation and block encoding of s-sparse matrices.
AI.motivation: Many quantum algorithms require coherent access to classical data, often modeled by quantum read-only memory (QROM). However, the actual cost of implementing sparse QROM—where only s of the 2^n addresses contain nonzero data—was not well understood. Characterizing the T-count (a key cost metric) of sparse QROM is essential for practical implementations of quantum algorithms that exploit data sparsity.
AI.method: The paper proves tight asymptotic T-count bounds Θ(√sm + √sn) for sparse QROM. Upper bounds are achieved via a multilevel hashing scheme that efficiently routes quantum queries to sparse addresses. Lower bounds are established by reducing sparse QROM to state preparation and using counting arguments over adaptive Clifford+T circuits, which remain valid even when mid-circuit measurements and classically controlled operations are permitted.
AI.result: The paper establishes asymptotically optimal T-count bounds Θ(√sm + √sn) for sparse QROM, and as corollaries obtains matching bounds Θ(√sn + √s log(1/ε) + log(1/ε)) for s-sparse state preparation and Θ(√(2^n sn) + √(2^n s log(s/ε_BE)) + log(s/ε_BE)) for block encoding of s-sparse matrices, where ε and ε_BE denote respective precisions.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a complete characterization of the T-count complexity of sparse QROM, showing a square-root dependence on both the support size and message length. The multilevel hashing upper bound and the counting-based lower bound match asymptotically, and the results naturally extend to tight bounds for sparse state preparation and sparse matrix block encoding.

title: No-Go Theorems for Quantum Transport Metrics from Fixed Cost Operators
summary: Coupling-based quantum optimal transport generalizes classical optimal transport by representing transport plans as bipartite states with prescribed marginals and evaluating their cost as the expectation of a fixed Hermitian operator. Friedland et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 110402 (2022)] conjectured that the square root of the optimal cost associated with the SWAP projector is a metric in every dimension and that this property persists for nearby quantum cost matrices. Miller [arXiv:2607.07764] disproved both conjectures by constructing explicit diagonal qutrit counterexamples. Building on his analysis, we prove a uniform no-go theorem for standard couplings. In every dimension $d\geq3$, no fixed cost operator makes either the optimal cost or its square root a metric, with violations occurring already among commuting states. The obstruction persists under stabilization of the SWAP cost. For channel-induced couplings, global nonnegativity and vanishing self-cost force the cost operator to be zero, precluding point separation when $d\geq2$. Taken together, these no-go results show that fixed-cost coupling formulations do not lead to metrics on the full quantum state space.

AI.tldr: The paper proves no-go theorems for coupling-based quantum optimal transport, showing that no fixed cost operator yields a metric (for either the cost or its square root) on the full quantum state space in dimensions d≥3, generalizing Miller's counterexamples, and that channel-induced couplings preclude metrics entirely in d≥2.
AI.motivation: Friedland et al. conjectured that the square root of the optimal cost associated with the SWAP projector is a metric in every dimension and that this property persists for nearby quantum cost matrices. Miller disproved both conjectures with diagonal qutrit counterexamples, and this work seeks to determine whether any fixed-cost coupling formulation can yield a metric, settling the question definitively via a uniform no-go theorem.
AI.method: Building on Miller's explicit diagonal qutrit counterexamples, the authors generalize the obstruction mechanism to prove a uniform no-go theorem for standard couplings by demonstrating metric violations among commuting states for any fixed cost operator in every dimension d≥3, including under stabilization of the SWAP cost. For channel-induced couplings, they show that global nonnegativity and vanishing self-cost force the cost operator to be identically zero, eliminating point separation for d≥2.
AI.result: No fixed cost operator makes either the optimal cost or its square root a metric in any dimension d≥3, with violations already occurring among commuting states. The obstruction persists even when stabilizing the SWAP cost. For channel-induced couplings, the cost operator must be zero, precluding point separation when d≥2.
AI.conclusion: Fixed-cost coupling formulations for quantum optimal transport—both standard and channel-induced—cannot yield metrics on the full quantum state space, requiring alternative approaches for defining quantum metric structure.

title: Noise-aware emulation and cross-device validation of neutral atom analog quantum processing units
summary: Analog quantum processors based on Rydberg atom arrays are a powerful platform for many-body quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and graph machine learning. As these devices become increasingly accessible, establishing confidence in their outputs requires predictive models that quantitatively connect microscopic hardware imperfections to empirical results. Here, we present a noise-aware emulation framework that propagates the dominant noise mechanisms throughout the full computation cycle to predict device behavior. We validate the framework by benchmarking two representative protocols, quantum annealing and post-quench dynamics, on three Pasqal quantum processors where classical simulations still provide ground truth. Across all three devices, the measured observables fall within the uncertainty envelopes predicted by the emulator. Beyond reproducing the data, the framework isolates which physical mechanism dominates in each operating regime, provides quantitative guidance for algorithm design and hardware improvements, and establishes a foundation for verifying analog processors in regimes beyond classical reach.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a noise-aware emulation framework for analog quantum processors based on Rydberg atom arrays. The framework propagates dominant noise mechanisms throughout the computation cycle to predict device behavior. It was validated on three Pasqal quantum processors using two protocols (quantum annealing and post-quench dynamics), with all measured observables falling within predicted uncertainty envelopes. The framework also identifies dominant physical mechanisms per operating regime and provides guidance for hardware improvements and algorithm design.
AI.motivation: As Rydberg atom array quantum processors become more accessible, there is a critical need for predictive models that quantitatively connect microscopic hardware imperfections to empirical results, establishing confidence in their outputs.
AI.method: A noise-aware emulation framework that propagates dominant noise mechanisms throughout the full computation cycle. The framework was validated by benchmarking two representative protocols (quantum annealing and post-quench dynamics) on three Pasqal quantum processors against classical simulation ground truths.
AI.result: Across all three devices, measured observables fell within the uncertainty envelopes predicted by the emulator. The framework successfully reproduced experimental data and isolated which physical mechanism dominates in each operating regime.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides quantitative guidance for algorithm design and hardware improvements, and establishes a foundation for verifying analog processors in regimes beyond classical reach.

title: Emergence of a Macroscopic Cat State and Multi-Channel Entanglement in a Frustrated Cluster Spin Chain
summary: We study a one-dimensional frustrated spin chain, which combines cluster-Ising and anisotropic next-nearest neighbor Ising models. We first offer a historical perspective that justifies the studied model. Then we study in detail the two quantum phases and prove that they are separated by a first order quantum phase transition. On one side, the ground state corresponds to a ferromagnetic phase, shows the presence of macroscopic cat states, and a small gap that closes in the thermodynamic limit. On the other phase, competing interactions avoid the establishment of a topological phase, though it conserves large incommensurate quantum correlations. We prove it is fundamentally distinct from a simple paramagnet, and we name it an incommensurate phase. This is a gapped phase, which gap does not close in the thermodynamic limit. While in the ferromagnetic phase there are two dominant Schmidt coefficients, in the incommensurate phase there are four. This corresponds to four distinct bipartite entanglement channels contributing substantially to the ground state. Finally, we discuss the utility of the macroscopic cat states for quantum metrology applications and the experimental feasibility of the system.

AI.tldr: The paper studies a one-dimensional frustrated spin chain combining cluster-Ising and anisotropic next-nearest neighbor Ising models, identifying two quantum phases separated by a first-order quantum phase transition: a ferromagnetic phase with macroscopic cat states and an incommensurate phase with large quantum correlations, distinguished by their Schmidt coefficients and entanglement structure.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to understand a frustrated spin model that combines cluster-Ising and anisotropic next-nearest neighbor Ising interactions, investigating its quantum phases and their properties, including potential applications for quantum metrology.
AI.method: The study analyzes a one-dimensional frustrated spin chain model via analytical proof of phase separation, examination of ground state properties including Schmidt coefficients, gap analysis in the thermodynamic limit, and evaluation of bipartite entanglement channels.
AI.result: Two quantum phases are identified: a ferromagnetic phase with macroscopic cat states, a closing gap in the thermodynamic limit, and two dominant Schmidt coefficients; and an incommensurate phase, which is gapped (gap does not close in the thermodynamic limit), distinct from a simple paramagnet, with four dominant Schmidt coefficients and four substantial bipartite entanglement channels.
AI.conclusion: The phases are separated by a first-order quantum phase transition. The ferromagnetic phase's macroscopic cat states may be useful for quantum metrology, and the system is experimentally feasible. The incommensurate phase holds large incommensurate quantum correlations fundamentally different from a paramagnet.

title: Counterdiabatic Driving under Variational Frame Dressing
summary: Counterdiabatic (CD) driving accelerates adiabatic protocols by prescribing auxiliary control fields, but often fails to map them to physically available operations. We derive a general formalism for such a mapping. We formulate CD driving in a variational dressed frame, where an unconstrained auxiliary generator reshapes the effective adiabatic problem while simultaneously forcing the applied correction to stay restricted to the native laboratory controls. This yields a laboratory-frame commutator equation that can be solved without constructing instantaneous eigenstates or the adiabatic and dressed-frame unitaries. The additional dressed-frame freedom reveals solutions that are inaccessible in the conventional adiabatic frame. We illustrate this mechanism in three settings: suppression of spectator errors in a multi-qubit chain driven by a single quadrature, an analytical acceleration of adiabatic Bell-state preparation with a fixed entangling interaction, and implementation of a fast adiabatic holonomic gate in a degenerate tripod manifold with correction pulses confined to the native couplings. Our results provide a systematic nonperturbative framework for constructing implementable counterdiabatic protocols beyond the conventional adiabatic frame.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a general variational dressed-frame formalism for counterdiabatic (CD) driving that maps auxiliary correction fields onto physically available laboratory controls, solving a commutator equation without requiring instantaneous eigenstates or adiabatic/dressed-frame unitaries. The framework is demonstrated in three settings: spectator-error suppression in a multi-qubit chain, accelerated adiabatic Bell-state preparation, and fast adiabatic holonomic gates in a degenerate tripod manifold, establishing a systematic nonperturbative approach to implementable CD protocols beyond the conventional adiabatic frame.
AI.motivation: Conventional counterdiabatic driving provides a powerful way to accelerate adiabatic protocols, but the auxiliary control fields it prescribes are often not physically realizable with the available lab controls. The paper addresses this fundamental gap by developing a general formalism that enforces the correction fields to stay within the set of native laboratory operations from the outset.
AI.method: The authors formulate CD driving in a variational dressed frame, where an unconstrained auxiliary generator both reshapes the effective adiabatic problem and constrains the applied correction to remain within native laboratory controls. This leads to a laboratory-frame commutator equation that bypasses the need to construct instantaneous eigenstates or adiabatic and dressed-frame unitaries. The added dressed-frame freedom produces solutions inaccessible in the conventional adiabatic frame.
AI.result: The formalism is validated through three illustrative settings: suppression of spectator errors in a multi-qubit chain driven by a single quadrature; analytical acceleration of adiabatic Bell-state preparation with a fixed entangling interaction; and implementation of a fast adiabatic holonomic gate in a degenerate tripod manifold with correction pulses restricted to native couplings.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a systematic, nonperturbative framework for constructing physically implementable counterdiabatic protocols, extending beyond what is possible in the conventional adiabatic frame by leveraging the variational freedom of the dressed frame.

title: Nearly optimal quantum circuits for Boolean oracles

AI.tldr: This paper proposes nearly optimal tradeoffs among circuit size, circuit depth, and ancilla count for quantum oracles implementing three kinds of Boolean functions: general total functions, partial functions with effective support size d, and sparse functions with true input size d. All bounds are asymptotically optimal up to logarithmic factors.
AI.motivation: Quantum oracles of Boolean functions bridge classical and quantum algorithms, but the circuit optimization of such oracles—particularly the tradeoffs among size, depth, and ancilla count—remains an open problem.
AI.method: The authors propose quantum circuit constructions achieving size–depth–ancilla tradeoffs for three classes of Boolean functions: general total functions (with 1 ≤ m ≤ Θ(2^n/n) ancilla), partial functions with effective support size d (with Θ(log d) ≤ m ≤ Θ(d) ancilla), and sparse functions with true input size d (with Θ(log n + log d) ≤ m ≤ Θ(nd/log d) ancilla). The resulting size and depth bounds are shown to be asymptotically optimal up to logarithmic factors.
AI.result: The paper achieves: (1) for general total Boolean functions with output size b and m ancilla, size O(b·2^n / log(n+m)) and depth O(b·2^n / (n+m)); (2) for partial Boolean functions, size O(n log d + bd) and depth O(n log n log d/(n+m) + log n + d(log d + b log m)/m); (3) for sparse Boolean functions, size O(n² log d + nd/log(log d + m/n)) and depth O(n² log n log d/(n+m) + log n + nd/m). All are asymptotically optimal up to logarithmic factors within their ancilla ranges.
AI.conclusion: The proposed quantum oracle constructions provide nearly optimal tradeoffs for circuit size, depth, and ancilla count across three classes of Boolean functions, with potential applications in embedding classical procedures into quantum circuits, such as QROM implementation and quantum algorithm design.

title: Improved Convergence of Carleman-Embedded Quantum Algorithm for the Vlasov-Poisson System
summary: We extend the regime of convergence of Carleman-embedded quantum algorithms that solve the Vlasov-Poisson equations from kinetic plasma physics. We establish convergence, using both analytical and numerical lower bounds, for physically reasonable collision frequencies using a Fourier-Hermite expansion of the shifted phase-space distribution function. We also show that for a large class of basis functions, the convergence of the Carleman-embedded Vlasov-Poisson system requires increasing collision frequency strength with velocity resolution. The complexity of the quantum algorithm depends strongly on whether we seek time-averaged or -resolved outputs.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the convergence regime of Carleman-embedded quantum algorithms for solving Vlasov-Poisson equations from kinetic plasma physics. Using a Fourier-Hermite expansion of the shifted phase-space distribution function, the authors establish convergence for physically reasonable collision frequencies via analytical and numerical lower bounds. They show that for a large class of basis functions, convergence requires increasing collision frequency strength with velocity resolution. The algorithm's complexity depends significantly on whether time-averaged or time-resolved outputs are sought.
AI.motivation: To broaden the applicability of Carleman-embedded quantum algorithms for Vlasov-Poisson equations by extending their convergence regime to physically realistic collision frequencies, which was previously limited or unclear.
AI.method: The authors use a Fourier-Hermite expansion of the shifted phase-space distribution function and employ both analytical and numerical lower bound analyses to establish convergence conditions. They also examine the dependence of convergence on basis function choice and collision frequency scaling with velocity resolution.
AI.result: Convergence is established for physically reasonable collision frequencies. It is shown that for a large class of basis functions, the convergence of the Carleman-embedded Vlasov-Poisson system requires collision frequency strength to increase with velocity resolution. The quantum algorithm's complexity differs substantially between time-averaged and time-resolved output scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The Carleman-embedded quantum algorithm for Vlasov-Poisson equations can converge for physically relevant collision parameters, but the collision frequency must scale with velocity resolution for broad classes of basis functions, and the algorithmic complexity is highly dependent on the type of output (time-averaged vs. time-resolved) required.

title: Classical Tensor Network and Quantum Fourier Transform Approaches for Large-Scale Carr-Madan Option Pricing
summary:
Fourier-based methods are among the most widely used techniques for pricing European options when the characteristic function of the underlying asset process is available. Their applicability to increasingly fine discretizations, however, is limited by the rapidly growing memory requirements of classical Fourier transforms, which become a computational bottleneck for large-scale pricing problems.
  In this work, we overcome this limitation by reformulating the Carr-Madan pricing framework using tensor networks. Specifically, we employ the Superfast Fourier Transform (SFFT), a compressed Tensor Train representation of the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT), and apply it directly to tensorized option pricing without ever explicitly constructing exponentially large vectors or Fourier operators. This formulation also enables a direct comparison between the classical tensor network algorithm and its quantum counterpart through QFT-based option pricing on quantum simulators and quantum hardware. Numerical experiments for European call options demonstrate that the proposed SFFT method maintains pricing accuracy while substantially reducing memory requirements and achieving subexponential computational scaling compared with conventional FFT-based pricing. The accompanying quantum simulations and hardware executions enable a direct comparison between the classical tensor network formulation and its QFT-based quantum counterpart, showing that both approaches avoid the exponential scaling of conventional Fourier implementations and provide complementary perspectives on large-scale option pricing.
  Together, these results establish a unified framework connecting classical Fourier pricing, tensor network algorithms, and quantum computing approaches, demonstrating how tensorized Fourier methods can provide scalable alternatives for high-dimensional financial computations.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates the Carr-Madan option pricing framework using tensor networks, specifically employing the Superfast Fourier Transform (SFFT)—a compressed Tensor Train representation of the Quantum Fourier Transform—to price European options without constructing exponentially large vectors or Fourier operators. The method maintains pricing accuracy while substantially reducing memory requirements and achieving subexponential computational scaling compared to conventional FFT-based pricing. The authors also compare the classical tensor network approach with quantum counterparts on simulators and hardware, establishing a unified framework connecting classical Fourier pricing, tensor networks, and quantum computing.
AI.motivation: Classical Fourier-based option pricing methods, while widely used, face a computational bottleneck: rapidly growing memory requirements of classical Fourier transforms when applied to increasingly fine discretizations, limiting their applicability to large-scale pricing problems.
AI.method: The authors reformulate the Carr-Madan pricing framework using tensor networks. They employ the Superfast Fourier Transform (SFFT), a compressed Tensor Train representation of the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT), applied directly to tensorized option pricing. This avoids explicitly constructing exponentially large vectors or Fourier operators, and enables direct comparison between classical tensor network algorithms and quantum counterparts via QFT-based pricing on quantum simulators and hardware.
AI.result: Numerical experiments for European call options show that the SFFT method maintains pricing accuracy while substantially reducing memory requirements and achieving subexponential computational scaling compared with conventional FFT-based pricing. Quantum simulations and hardware executions demonstrate both classical tensor network and QFT-based quantum approaches avoid the exponential scaling of conventional Fourier implementations.
AI.conclusion: The results establish a unified framework connecting classical Fourier pricing, tensor network algorithms, and quantum computing approaches, demonstrating that tensorized Fourier methods can provide scalable alternatives for high-dimensional financial computations.

title: Quantum Steering and Nonlocal Correlations Between Non-Interacting Delocalized Electrons Under Rashba Spin-Orbit Interaction
summary: We investigate quantum steering and nonlocal correlations between two electrons in a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) as functions of Rashba spin-orbit interaction (RSOI) strength and inter-electron separation. We focus particularly on the Bi/Ag(111) system characterized by its strong RSOI ($α_0 = 3.05\times10^{-11}$ eV~m), and we explore the influence of tuning intensity of RSOI and inter-electron distance on the dynamics of Bell nonlocality, uncertainty-induced nonlocality and steering. We find that, although increasing $α_R$ initially suppresses quantum correlations, all three metrics exhibit a non-monotonic recovery as functions of $α_R$, peaking near an optimal coupling strength $α_R = 4.32\times10^{-11}$~eV~m across the range of inter-electron separations considered. This finding establishes RSOI as a critical control parameter for stabilizing quantum properties in two-dimensional electron gases against the decay of quantum correlations with inter-electron separation, and shows that the suppression and recovery of quantum resources within the Bi/Ag(111) system can be controlled by adjusting the inter-electron distance and carefully tuning the RSOI strength.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates quantum steering, Bell nonlocality, and uncertainty-induced nonlocality between two electrons in a 2DEG, specifically the Bi/Ag(111) system, as functions of Rashba spin-orbit interaction strength and inter-electron separation. Despite initial suppression of quantum correlations with increasing α_R, all three metrics show non-monotonic recovery, peaking near an optimal RSOI strength of 4.32×10⁻¹¹ eV·m, establishing RSOI as a control parameter for stabilizing quantum properties in 2DEGs.
AI.motivation: To understand how Rashba spin-orbit interaction can serve as a control parameter for regulating and stabilizing quantum correlations (steering, Bell nonlocality, uncertainty-induced nonlocality) in two-dimensional electron gases, particularly in the strong-RSOI Bi/Ag(111) system, against decoherence caused by increasing inter-electron separation.
AI.method: The study analyzes three quantum correlation metrics—Bell nonlocality, uncertainty-induced nonlocality, and quantum steering—between two electrons in a 2DEG as functions of RSOI strength (α_R) and inter-electron separation. The Bi/Ag(111) system with characteristic strong RSOI (α₀ = 3.05×10⁻¹¹ eV·m) is the focal system, with systematic variation of α_R and inter-electron distance to map the full behavior of quantum correlations.
AI.result: Increasing α_R initially suppresses quantum correlations, but all three metrics exhibit non-monotonic recovery as functions of α_R, peaking near an optimal coupling strength of α_R = 4.32×10⁻¹¹ eV·m across all considered inter-electron separations. This shows quantum resource suppression and recovery can be controlled by tuning both inter-electron distance and RSOI strength.
AI.conclusion: Rashba spin-orbit interaction is a critical control parameter for stabilizing quantum properties in 2DEGs against the decay of quantum correlations with inter-electron separation. The Bi/Ag(111) system offers tunable control over quantum resources (steering and nonlocality) by adjusting inter-electron distance and RSOI strength, with an optimal RSOI coupling that maximizes these correlations.

title: Mitigating quantum decoherence via global optimal control
summary: We show that global optimal control can drastically suppress the impact of decoherence in globally driven superconducting quantum computing architectures, taking as a prototype a recently proposed quasi-two-dimensional ladder geometry. Using a tensor-network-based approach, we quantify how amplitude-damping and dephasing channels degrade the flow of quantum information along the ladder and the fidelity of one- and two-qubit gate operations. We then demonstrate that shaping the global drive compresses the gate sequences by an order of magnitude in time, restoring high gate fidelities. We stress that this mitigation is far from trivial: in a globally driven processor, dissipation acts on every physical qubit---including those outside the logical register that sustain the surrounding ordered phases---so its impact cannot be suppressed by protecting an isolated subsystem, and is instead overcome purely through the temporal shaping of the global drive.

AI.tldr: Global optimal control can drastically suppress decoherence effects in globally driven superconducting quantum computing architectures, demonstrated on a quasi-two-dimensional ladder geometry, by compressing gate sequences an order of magnitude in time and restoring high gate fidelities.
AI.motivation: In globally driven superconducting quantum processors, dissipation affects every physical qubit—including those outside the logical register—so decoherence cannot be mitigated by protecting an isolated subsystem. The authors aim to quantify and overcome this decoherence impact through temporal shaping of the global drive.
AI.method: The authors use a tensor-network-based approach to quantify how amplitude-damping and dephasing channels degrade quantum information flow along a quasi-two-dimensional ladder geometry and the fidelity of one- and two-qubit gate operations. They then apply global optimal control to shape the global drive, compressing gate sequences by an order of magnitude in time.
AI.result: Shaping the global drive compresses gate sequences by an order of magnitude in time, restoring high gate fidelities and drastically suppressing the impact of decoherence.
AI.conclusion: Decoherence mitigation in globally driven quantum processors can be achieved purely through temporal shaping of the global drive, without isolating or protecting individual subsystems, demonstrating that global optimal control is an effective and non-trivial strategy for suppressing dissipation.

title: Optical linewidth narrowing for device-coupled single T centers
summary: Single T centers in silicon have emerged as promising optically active spins for quantum networking applications. One of the major obstacles to advancing the system is their broad optical linewidth due to spectral diffusion, which is two orders of magnitude larger than their cavity-enhanced radiative linewidth. We tackle this issue by utilizing above-band optical excitation delivered via a laser scanning microscope to device-coupled single T centers, achieving up to 70% optical linewidth reduction. We attribute the linewidth narrowing effect to the filling of nearby charge traps by photo-generated free carriers. We analyze charge stabilization dynamics by exploiting pulsed above-band excitation and develop a rate equation model to describe the dynamics and to explain the observed linewidth narrowing and center shift. This work provides an effective pathway to control and reduce the optical linewidth for single T centers, clearing one of the major roadblocks to advance the single T center spin platform for quantum information and networking applications.

AI.tldr: The paper demonstrates that above-band optical excitation via a laser scanning microscope reduces spectral diffusion-induced optical linewidth broadening in single T centers in silicon by up to 70%, attributing the effect to charge trap filling by photo-generated free carriers. A rate equation model is developed to describe the charge stabilization dynamics and explain the linewidth narrowing and center shift, providing a pathway to overcome a major obstacle for the T center spin platform in quantum networking.
AI.motivation: Single T centers in silicon are promising optically active spins for quantum networking, but their optical linewidth is ~100x broader than the cavity-enhanced radiative limit due to spectral diffusion, which is a major obstacle to system advancement.
AI.method: The authors use above-band optical excitation delivered via a laser scanning microscope to device-coupled single T centers. They exploit pulsed above-band excitation to analyze charge stabilization dynamics and develop a rate equation model to describe the dynamics, linewidth narrowing, and center shifts.
AI.result: Up to 70% optical linewidth reduction was achieved. The narrowing is attributed to the filling of nearby charge traps by photo-generated free carriers, and the rate equation model successfully captures the observed dynamics.
AI.conclusion: This work provides an effective pathway to control and reduce the optical linewidth for single T centers, removing one of the critical roadblocks to advancing single T center spin platforms for quantum information and networking applications.

title: Generating broadband optical squeezing via Cascaded Micro-Ring Resonators
summary: Broadband squeezed light functioning as a Markovian reservoir can exponentially enhance light-matter interactions, benefiting quantum technologies. However, conventional single-cavity sources face a trade-off between squeezing depth and spectral bandwidth. We propose a scalable scheme for generating broadband squeezed vacuum using a cascade of parametric microring resonators coupled to a common bus waveguide. By analyzing the output, we identify the specific conditions that yield a broad, flat-topped squeezing spectrum, even under realistic intracavity pump attenuation. We demonstrate that this architecture is robust against fabrication imperfections, including inhomogeneous resonator frequencies and component failures. We show that the flat-topped spectrum converges to the Markovian limit significantly faster than a single-cavity Lorentzian profile. An array of as few as $N=5$ coupled resonators with an intrinsic loss ratio of $κ_I/κ= 0.1$ reduces the required bandwidth to a quarter of that needed by a single cavity to achieve same squeezing. This rapid convergence relaxes the low-$Q$ and high-gain constraints of single broadband cavities, distributing the squeezing process across moderately pumped resonators to provide a practical route for engineering squeezed reservoirs on mature integrated photonic platforms.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a scalable scheme for generating broadband squeezed vacuum using a cascade of parametric microring resonators coupled to a common bus waveguide. An array of as few as N=5 resonators can reduce the required bandwidth to a quarter of that needed by a single cavity while achieving the same squeezing, converging to the Markovian limit significantly faster than single-cavity Lorentzian profiles.
AI.motivation: Broadband squeezed light acting as a Markovian reservoir can exponentially enhance light-matter interactions, but conventional single-cavity sources face an inherent trade-off between squeezing depth and spectral bandwidth, limiting practical realization on integrated photonic platforms.
AI.method: The authors propose a cascade of parametric microring resonators coupled to a common bus waveguide. They analyze the output to identify conditions yielding a broad, flat-topped squeezing spectrum, considering realistic intracavity pump attenuation and testing robustness against fabrication imperfections such as inhomogeneous resonator frequencies and component failures.
AI.result: The flat-topped spectrum converges to the Markovian limit significantly faster than a single-cavity Lorentzian profile. An array of N=5 coupled resonators with intrinsic loss ratio κ_I/κ=0.1 reduces required bandwidth to a quarter of that needed by a single cavity for equal squeezing. The architecture is robust against fabrication imperfections and component failures.
AI.conclusion: The cascade architecture relaxes the low-Q and high-gain constraints of single broadband cavities by distributing the squeezing process across moderately pumped resonators, providing a practical route for engineering squeezed reservoirs on mature integrated photonic platforms.

title: Structure-Preserving Quantum Simulation of Wave Equations on a Trapped-Ion Processor
summary: Wave equations provide a natural testbed for near-term quantum simulation of partial differential equations, but hardware demonstrations have remained limited in spatial dimension, equation class, system size, and physically meaningful output. We develop and benchmark structure-preserving, Fourier-based quantum circuits for the one- and two dimensional acoustic wave equations and Dirac dynamics with variable mass on the Quantinuum H2-2 trapped-ion processor. The experiments include one-dimensional grids with up to \(1024\) points and \(32\times32\) two-dimensional grids, corresponding to an encoded state-space dimension of up to \(4096\). Rather than reconstructing the full fields, we estimate subdomain kinetic energies directly from measurement samples. Across all tested acoustic and Dirac dynamics problems, the H2-2 results track the classical kinetic-energy dynamics with mean absolute errors between \(5.9\times10^{-3}\) and \(2.4\times10^{-2}\). At fixed retained bandwidth, the compiled gate counts grow approximately quadratically with the number of grid qubits; the acoustic circuit sizes are essentially independent of evolution time, whereas the cost also grows with the number of product-formula steps. These results provide hardware-level evidence that accurate observable dynamics can remain resolvable for structured wave problems with thousands of encoded degrees of freedom on a present-day trapped-ion processor.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates and benchmarks structure-preserving Fourier-based quantum circuits for 1D and 2D acoustic wave equations and Dirac dynamics on the Quantinuum H2-2 trapped-ion processor, achieving accurate kinetic-energy observable dynamics for systems up to 4096 encoded degrees of freedom with mean absolute errors between 5.9×10⁻³ and 2.4×10⁻².
AI.motivation: Wave equations offer a natural testbed for near-term quantum simulation of partial differential equations, yet prior hardware demonstrations have been limited in spatial dimension, equation class, system size, and physically meaningful output. The authors aim to address these gaps by providing hardware-level evidence that accurate observable dynamics can remain resolvable for structured wave problems with thousands of encoded degrees of freedom on a present-day trapped-ion processor.
AI.method: The authors develop structure-preserving, Fourier-based quantum circuits for 1D and 2D acoustic wave equations and Dirac dynamics with variable mass. Experiments are run on the Quantinuum H2-2 trapped-ion processor, covering 1D grids up to 1024 points and 32×32 2D grids (up to 4096-dimensional state space). Instead of reconstructing full fields, they estimate subdomain kinetic energies directly from measurement samples. They also analyze gate-count scaling with grid qubits and evolution time.
AI.result: Across all tested acoustic and Dirac dynamics problems, H2-2 results track classical kinetic-energy dynamics with mean absolute errors between 5.9×10⁻³ and 2.4×10⁻². Compiled gate counts grow approximately quadratically with the number of grid qubits at fixed retained bandwidth; acoustic circuit sizes are essentially independent of evolution time, whereas Dirac cost grows with the number of product-formula steps.
AI.conclusion: The results provide hardware-level evidence that accurate observable dynamics can remain resolvable for structured wave problems with thousands of encoded degrees of freedom on a present-day trapped-ion processor, extending the practical reach of near-term quantum simulation for PDEs.

title: Spacetime Layout and Logical Compilation of Color Code
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires system-level coordination of logical primitives. Here, we establish a logical compilation framework for the color code, grounded in its topological structure and supporting universal logical operations. Based on its anyon-condensation and domain-wall structure, we introduce a spacetime block-diagram representation capturing logical patches and operations and derive the rules governing block assembly. A correspondence with ZX diagrams further identifies the logical semantics of this representation and enables transformations that preserve the represented computation. Moreover, we develop a code-derived compilation strategy that converts ZX representations of logical computations into valid color-code spacetime layouts. In this strategy, edge-decorated ZX diagrams tailor the logical representation to the color code under the block-assembly constraints, and fusion-region-aware routing exploits semantic equivalence during geometric embedding. We automate the complete logical compilation process and demonstrate successful compilation across a broad range of algorithms. Our work advances color-code architecture from individual primitives to the automated synthesis of logical computations, marking a significant step toward its full-stack quantum computing.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a logical compilation framework for color-code quantum computing, using spacetime block-diagram representations grounded in anyon-condensation and domain-wall structure, with ZX-diagram correspondences for semantic preservation. It introduces code-derived compilation strategies (edge-decorated ZX diagrams and fusion-region-aware routing) and demonstrates automated compilation across a broad range of quantum algorithms.
AI.motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires system-level coordination of logical primitives, but color-code architectures have largely been developed at the level of individual primitives. There is a need for an automated, full-stack compilation framework that translates logical computations into valid color-code spacetime layouts.
AI.method: The authors develop a logical compilation framework grounded in color-code topology. They introduce a spacetime block-diagram representation capturing logical patches and operations, derive block-assembly rules based on anyon-condensation and domain-wall structure, and establish a correspondence with ZX diagrams for logical semantics. A code-derived compilation strategy converts edge-decorated ZX representations into valid color-code spacetime layouts, with fusion-region-aware routing exploiting semantic equivalence during geometric embedding. The complete process is automated.
AI.result: The framework successfully compiles a broad range of algorithms into valid color-code spacetime layouts, demonstrating that logical compilation from algorithmic descriptions to hardware-level color-code architectures can be fully automated.
AI.conclusion: This work advances color-code quantum computing from isolated logical primitives to automated synthesis of complete logical computations, marking a significant step toward full-stack, fault-tolerant quantum computing based on the color code.

title: Spectral gaps of ironed two-qubit gadgets matching the iSWAP gap
summary: We prove that every ironed two-qubit gadget whose KAK-derived parameter satisfies $a=5/9$ has, on the complete graph $K_n$ with $n\geqslant 5$, the same second-moment spectral gap as the iSWAP gadget. The central step is a representation-theoretic localisation theorem: the largest strictly negative eigenvalue of the associated $\mathfrak S_n$-invariant operator always occurs in the highest-spin $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ summand. A local positive-semidefinite decomposition separates every spin sector except the two highest. This settles a conjecture of Kong, Li, and Liu.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that any ironed two-qubit gadget with KAK parameter a=5/9 has the same second-moment spectral gap as the iSWAP gadget on complete graphs K_n (n≥5), settling a conjecture of Kong, Li, and Liu.
AI.motivation: To settle a conjecture by Kong, Li, and Liu regarding the spectral gap equivalence between ironed two-qubit gadgets with a specific KAK parameter and the iSWAP gadget on complete graphs.
AI.method: The proof relies on a representation-theoretic localisation theorem showing that the largest strictly negative eigenvalue of the S_n-invariant operator occurs in the highest-spin SU(2) summand. A local positive-semidefinite decomposition separates every spin sector except the two highest.
AI.result: It is proven that every ironed two-qubit gadget with a=5/9 has the same second-moment spectral gap as the iSWAP gadget on K_n with n≥5, confirming the conjecture.
AI.conclusion: The conjecture of Kong, Li, and Liu is settled via a representation-theoretic localisation theorem and a positive-semidefinite decomposition technique.

title: When quantum thermal states look classical
summary: At high temperature, quantum Gibbs states retain several classical features of the maximally mixed state: the absence of entanglement, the absence of magic, analyticity of the partition function, correlation decay, and algorithmic tractability. We prove new and sharp bounds showing that these features persist down to finite temperatures independent of system size, but fail at distinct inverse-temperature scales, forming a hierarchy of classical-to-quantum transitions. Our results hold for long-range Pauli interactions with bounded strength at every site. Despite such all-to-all interactions, we show that the death of entanglement occurs at constant temperature, resolving an open question of Rouze, Franca and Alhambra (STOC'25). We give a polynomial-time classical algorithm that prepares Gibbs states up to the death of entanglement transition. Notably, this is asymptotically colder than temperatures at which quantum Gibbs samplers are known to mix quickly, as well as the original separability temperature of Bakshi et al. (FOCS'24), which we improve to be tight up to constants. At asymptotically even colder temperatures, we show that the Gibbs state remains in the thermodynamic infinite-temperature phase. This leads to polynomial-time classical algorithms for estimating thermal expectations despite both entanglement and magic, and the resolution of a correlation decay conjecture of Harrow, Mehraban and Soleimanifar (STOC'20).

AI.tldr: This paper proves sharp bounds showing that classical features of quantum Gibbs states (no entanglement, no magic, analytic partition function, correlation decay, algorithmic tractability) persist down to finite temperatures independent of system size for long-range Pauli interactions. These features fail at distinct inverse-temperature scales, forming a hierarchy of classical-to-quantum transitions. The authors resolve two open problems: the death of entanglement occurs at constant temperature (answering Rouze, Franca, Alhambra, STOC'25), and a correlation decay conjecture (Harrow, Mehraban, Soleimanifar, STOC'20). They provide polynomial-time classical algorithms for Gibbs state preparation down to the entanglement transition and for estimating thermal expectations even at temperatures where both entanglement and magic exist.
AI.motivation: To understand the precise temperature scales at which quantum Gibbs states lose their classical features (entanglement-freeness, magic-freeness, analyticity, correlation decay, classical tractability) for long-range interacting systems, and to resolve open questions about separability thresholds and correlation decay in such systems.
AI.method: The paper analyzes quantum Gibbs states of long-range Pauli interactions with bounded strength per site, deriving sharp bounds on the inverse-temperature scales at which distinct classical features (no entanglement, no magic, analytic partition function, correlation decay, classical algorithmic tractability) break down. It uses analytic and combinatorial techniques to establish a hierarchy of transition temperatures and constructs polynomial-time classical algorithms for Gibbs state preparation and thermal expectation estimation.
AI.result: The authors prove that entanglement death occurs at constant temperature (independent of system size), resolving an open question from STOC'25. They provide a polynomial-time classical algorithm for preparing Gibbs states down to this entanglement transition, which is asymptotically colder than known quantum Gibbs sampler mixing temperatures and improves the separability bound of Bakshi et al. (FOCS'24) to be tight up to constants. At even colder temperatures, the Gibbs state remains in the infinite-temperature thermodynamic phase, enabling polynomial-time classical estimation of thermal expectations despite presence of entanglement and magic, and resolving a correlation decay conjecture from STOC'20.
AI.conclusion: For long-range Pauli interactions, the classical features of quantum Gibbs states fail at distinct temperature scales, establishing a well-separated hierarchy of classical-to-quantum transitions. Constant-temperature entanglement death is confirmed, and classical algorithms remain efficient in regimes previously thought to require quantum methods, resolving multiple open problems in the field.

title: A Provable Oracle-Free Quantum Algorithm for Nonlinear Dynamics on Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Processors
summary: We develop a hybrid qubit--qumode algorithm for nonlinear ordinary differential equations of the form $\dot{\mathbf{x}}=\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})$ with drift of polynomial degree~$L$. Following the Fokker--Planck route of Tennie and Magri, the algorithm propagates the state density and returns the deterministic trajectory as the peak of that density in the small-noise limit. The discretised generator is carried into a parametrised family of Schrödinger equations by the warped-phase transformation of Jin, Liu, and Yu, and the Fourier-mode parameter of that family is placed on a single continuous-variable qumode. Our central structural result is that the Hermitian parts $H_{1}$ and $H_{2}$ of the discretised generator admit a bipartite Pauli decomposition that sorts the non-zero Pauli strings into $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ mutually commuting families and factorises each family into a diagonal of degree at most $L$ tensored with a fixed rank-two bond operator. The factorisation renders each family exponential an exact product of $\mathcal{O}(n^{L})$ monomial-controlled momentum displacements, with no intra-family Trotter error. On a $d$-dimensional grid of $N=2^{n}$ points per axis the circuit costs $\mathcal{O}(d^{L+1}n^{L+2})$ gates per Trotter step. No sparse-access oracle and no block encoding is invoked: every gate is fixed in closed form by the polynomial coefficients of the drift. We also prove a bound on the numerical abscissa $λ_{\max}(H_{1})$ that fixes the recovery domain of the warped-phase transform and the post-selection cost. A classical simulation on two nonlinear benchmarks confirms the structural theorems, the shifted recovery, and the accuracy-per-resource advantage of the continuous-variable coupling over a discretised mode register.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a hybrid qubit-qumode algorithm for nonlinear ODEs of polynomial drift, propagating the state density via the Fokker-Planck equation and recovering deterministic trajectories in the small-noise limit. A warped-phase transformation converts the discretised generator into a parametrised family of Schrödinger equations with the Fourier-mode parameter encoded on a single continuous-variable qumode. The key structural result is a bipartite Pauli decomposition sorting non-zero Pauli strings into O(log N) mutually commuting families, each factorised into a diagonal tensor a rank-two bond operator, enabling exact product-form exponentiation with no intra-family Trotter error. The circuit costs O(d^{L+1}n^{L+2}) gates per Trotter step on a d-dimensional grid, requires no sparse-access oracle or block encoding (all gates fixed in closed form from polynomial coefficients), and a bound on the numerical abscissa fixes the recovery domain and post-selection cost. Classical simulations on two nonlinear benchmarks confirm the structural theorems and the accuracy-per-resource advantage of continuous-variable coupling.
AI.motivation: To develop an efficient quantum algorithm for solving nonlinear ordinary differential equations with polynomial drift, avoiding the need for sparse-access oracles and block encodings by leveraging a hybrid qubit-qumode architecture and the Fokker-Planck / warped-phase formalism.
AI.method: The algorithm propagates a state density via the Fokker-Planck equation (Tennie-Magri route), applies the warped-phase transformation (Jin-Liu-Yu) to convert the discretised generator into a parametrised family of Schrödinger equations, and encodes the Fourier-mode parameter on a single continuous-variable qumode. The central tool is a bipartite Pauli decomposition proving the Hermitian parts admit O(log N) mutually commuting families, each factorised into a diagonal (degree ≤ L) tensored with a rank-two bond operator, allowing exact product-form exponentiation via monomial-controlled momentum displacements.
AI.result: The circuit cost is O(d^{L+1}n^{L+2}) gates per Trotter step on a d-dimensional grid of N=2^n points per axis, with no sparse-access oracle or block encoding. A bound on the numerical abscissa λ_max(H1) establishes the recovery domain of the warped-phase transform and post-selection cost. Classical simulations on two nonlinear benchmarks confirm the structural theorems, shifted recovery, and superior accuracy-per-resource of continuous-variable coupling over a discretised mode register.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid qubit-qumode algorithm provides an efficient, oracle-free approach to nonlinear ODEs with polynomial drift, with provable circuit cost scaling, structural commutation properties enabling exact exponential factorisation, and validated performance on benchmark problems.

title: Statistically secure uncloneable encryption of arbitrary messages
summary: Unconditional uncloneable encryption of a single bit with efficient encryption and decryption is now possible. However, whether the extension to messages of arbitrary length achieves statistical security remains to be known. Using the fact that the encoding bases for the single-bit scheme known to be secure consist of a subset of the Clifford unitaries, we show that this scheme can be upgraded to achieve unconditional uncloneable encryption for messages of arbitrary length, with encoding time polynomial in the message length and security parameter. This establishes that one-time uncloneable encryption of arbitrary messages enjoys statistical security.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that uncloneable encryption can be extended from single bits to messages of arbitrary length, achieving unconditional (statistical) security with efficient (polynomial-time) encoding and decoding.
AI.motivation: Previous work achieved uncloneable encryption for a single bit with statistical security, but it was unknown whether this could be extended to arbitrary-length messages while maintaining unconditional security.
AI.method: The authors leverage the fact that the encoding bases used in the secure single-bit scheme are a subset of the Clifford unitaries. Using this property, they upgrade the single-bit scheme to an arbitrary-length message scheme.
